canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.name: Sweetleaf Soup with Egg
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.serving_basis: One pot of soup to share among four people as part of a family meal.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.description: Lightly bruised sweetleaf is simmered with egg for a green, fragrant soup with natural sweetness. This streamlined home version adds beaten egg while the broth gently simmers so it forms soft ribbons and the leaves stay tender.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.finished_dish: Clear broth with tender green leaves and delicate, fully cooked egg ribbons; mild and savory.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.serving: Ladle into a bowl while hot and serve with steamed rice and a main dish or lightly stir-fried vegetables.
tips: Bruise the leaves gently; crushing them can make the broth cloudy.
Drizzle the egg into gently simmering soup and stir in one direction for soft ribbons.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.image_alt: Sweetleaf soup with egg in a white porcelain bowl, showing green leaves and soft golden egg ribbons.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.time_note: About 20 minutes; add the leaves near the end to preserve their green color and tenderness.

ingredients.name: Sweetleaf
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh, undamaged leaves and strip the tender leaves from the stems.

ingredients.name: Chicken eggs
ingredients.notes: Beat gently before adding.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Pork fat can be used instead to suit household preference.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the preferred soup consistency.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season gradually, then taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust to account for the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the soup before serving.

preparation_steps: Pick over and rinse the sweetleaf thoroughly, then drain. Gently bruise a handful of leaves.
Peel and mince the shallot. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt; wash hands and tools after handling raw egg.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and briefly saute the shallot until fragrant. Add the greens and stir for about one minute, then pour in the water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a gentle simmer and season with fish sauce and salt. Drizzle in the egg while stirring gently; cook until the egg is fully set.
Taste, turn off the heat as soon as the greens are tender, ladle into a bowl and finish with pepper.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-trung.media_alt_text: A bowl of Vietnamese sweet-leaf soup with soft egg ribbons and green leaves.

ga-hap-la-chanh.name: Steamed Chicken with Vietnamese Lime Leaves
ga-hap-la-chanh.serving_basis: One chicken of about 1.2 kg, cut into serving pieces for four people.
ga-hap-la-chanh.description: Vietnamese free-range chicken is steamed over lemongrass and lime leaves, keeping the meat juicy while perfuming its lightly golden skin. This home-kitchen version uses a simple salt base and is served with lime-pepper salt so the citrus-leaf aroma remains distinct.
ga-hap-la-chanh.finished_dish: Evenly cooked chicken with pale-golden skin, moist meat and a gentle lemongrass and lime-leaf aroma; no pink remains near the bone.
ga-hap-la-chanh.serving: Cut into bite-size pieces, scatter with fine lime-leaf strips and serve hot with lime-pepper salt, rice or boiled greens.
tips: Drain the chicken well after rinsing so excess water does not dilute its flavor.
Check that the thickest part reaches 74°C and use a clean platter after cooking.
ga-hap-la-chanh.image_alt: Vietnamese lime-leaf steamed chicken pieces on a white platter with lemongrass and lime leaves.
ga-hap-la-chanh.time_note: About 75 minutes including a 10-minute seasoning rest; steaming time depends on the chicken's size.

ingredients.name: Free-range chicken
ingredients.notes: Clean and drain; steam whole or halved to fit the pot.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Rinse and bruise the stalks.

ingredients.name: Lime leaves
ingredients.notes: Divide between the steaming bed and garnish.

ingredients.name: Coarse salt
ingredients.notes: Dry-roast and spread in a thin layer at the bottom of the pot.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice and layer with lemongrass.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Rub over the chicken, then rinse clean.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use some for seasoning and some for the dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Squeeze for the dipping salt.

preparation_steps: Rub the chicken with salt, rinse and pat dry. Season lightly with pepper and rest for 10 minutes; keep it separate from ready-to-eat foods.
Rinse the lemongrass and lime leaves. Bruise the lemongrass, finely slice a few leaves for garnish and prepare a covered steamer.
cooking_steps: Dry-roast the coarse salt in a heavy pot for about five minutes. Turn off the heat and layer the lemongrass, ginger and some lime leaves over it.
Place the chicken on the aromatic layer, add the remaining leaves, cover tightly and steam over medium heat. A 1.2 kg chicken usually takes 40–45 minutes.
Check that the thickest part reaches 74°C. Rest for five minutes, cut into pieces, garnish with lime leaves and serve with lime-pepper salt.
ga-hap-la-chanh.media_alt_text: Sliced steamed chicken with lemongrass and finely shredded lime leaves on a ceramic plate.

canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.name: Vietnamese Crab Soup with Jute Leaves, Malabar Spinach and Luffa
aliases: Crab Soup with Jute Leaves and Malabar Spinach
Vietnamese Field Crab and Luffa Soup
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.serving_basis: One summer crab soup with seasonal greens to share among four people.
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.description: Freshwater crab forms soft savory curds in a clear broth with jute leaves, Malabar spinach and fragrant luffa. This is a familiar Northern Vietnamese summer soup, served with hot rice and lightly fermented pickled eggplant; using ready-ground crab makes home preparation easier.
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.finished_dish: Soft crab curds, gently sweet broth and tender greens; the luffa is just cooked and holds its shape.
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.serving: Ladle carefully to keep the crab curds intact. Serve hot with rice and, if desired, lightly fermented pickled eggplant.
tips: Keep ready-ground crab chilled until cooking and strain it to remove shell fragments.
Use medium heat and avoid stirring once the crab curds begin to set.
search_terms: Vietnamese crab soup with jute leaves
crab soup with Malabar spinach and luffa
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.image_alt: A bowl of Vietnamese freshwater crab soup with a crab curd, green leaves and luffa.
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.time_note: About 45 minutes when using ground crab; preparing whole crabs takes longer.

ingredients.name: Ground freshwater crab
ingredients.notes: Buy freshly ground crab and keep chilled; strain thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use to dilute and strain the crab.

ingredients.name: Jute leaves
ingredients.notes: Pick tender leaves, rinse and chop coarsely.

ingredients.name: Malabar spinach
ingredients.notes: Pick tender leaves and tips, then rinse.

ingredients.name: Fragrant luffa
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into 1 cm slices.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Mince; optional for a cleaner crab flavor.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Optional, for briefly cooking the crab roe with shallot.

preparation_steps: If using whole crabs, soak and rinse them well, remove the apron and gills, reserve the roe, then grind the bodies with salt and water.
Strain the crab mixture through a fine sieve and discard the shell residue. Rinse and chop the greens, then peel and slice the luffa.
cooking_steps: Pour the strained crab liquid into a pot. Heat over medium, stirring gently at first; once the curds rise, stop stirring and lift them into a clean bowl.
If using roe, briefly saute it with shallot and return it to the pot. Season with salt, add the luffa, then add both greens when the broth boils.
Cook just until the greens are tender, return the crab curds to the pot and turn off the heat. Serve hot; avoid prolonged reheating.
canh-cua-rau-day-mong-toi-muop.media_alt_text: A bowl of field-crab soup with crab roe, jute leaves, Malabar spinach and luffa.

dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.name: Vegetarian Braised Tofu with Straw Mushrooms
aliases: Vietnamese Vegetarian Tofu and Straw Mushroom Hot Pot
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.serving_basis: One pot of braised tofu and straw mushrooms to share with rice among four people.
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.description: Lightly browned tofu and tender straw mushrooms simmer in soy-seasoned broth until flavorful while keeping their shape. This simple vegetarian family dish uses Vietnamese leek in place of shallot and pairs naturally with steamed rice and boiled greens.
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.finished_dish: Tofu is tender inside with a lightly seared surface; mushrooms stay plump and the soy sauce reduces to a glossy, peppery glaze.
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.serving: Spoon the tofu, mushrooms and sauce into a small serving pot, finish with pepper and green leek, and serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Choose young button-stage straw mushrooms and rinse them quickly so they do not absorb excess water.
Turn the pot gently instead of stirring vigorously to keep the tofu intact; check labels on seasonings for vegan suitability.
search_terms: vegetarian braised tofu with straw mushrooms
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.image_alt: Golden tofu braised with straw mushrooms in a Vietnamese clay pot with glossy soy sauce and pepper.
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.time_note: About 35 minutes; braise gently until the sauce coats the tofu and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Firm white tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into bite-size cubes and pat dry.

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the stems, rinse quickly and halve larger mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese leek
ingredients.notes: Finely slice and separate the white and green parts.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For searing the tofu and sauteing the leek.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a variety suitable for your dietary requirements.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to adjust sauce consistency.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the saltiness of the soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Check the ingredients if following a strict vegan diet.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the dish before serving.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; slice before adding.

preparation_steps: Cut the tofu into bite-size pieces and blot away excess moisture. Clean the mushrooms, halve the larger ones, rinse the leek and slice it.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, vegetarian seasoning, pepper and water. Taste for a gently savory-sweet balance.
cooking_steps: Heat half the oil and sear both sides of the tofu until lightly golden; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to a pot and saute the white part of the leek. Add the mushrooms and stir for about two minutes, then add the tofu and sauce mixture.
Braise over low heat for 10–12 minutes, gently swirling the pot instead of stirring hard. Once the sauce lightly thickens, adjust the seasoning, add green leek and chili, then turn off the heat.
dau-hu-kho-nam-rom-chay.media_alt_text: Golden tofu braised with straw mushrooms in a glossy soy sauce, finished with black pepper.

ga-nau-dau.name: Vietnamese chicken and mixed-bean stew
aliases: Chicken stew with red beans and soybeans
ga-nau-dau.serving_basis: About 400 g chicken simmered with 100 g soybeans and red beans for four people.
ga-nau-dau.description: Chicken is browned and simmered with soybeans, red beans and carrot until the beans are tender. This family-style dish has a lightly thickened broth and works with rice or bread; soak the beans ahead of time.
ga-nau-dau.finished_dish: Tender chicken, soft but intact beans, just-cooked carrot and a gentle garlic-pepper broth.
ga-nau-dau.serving: Ladle into a bowl; finish with scallions, Vietnamese coriander and pepper. Serve hot with rice or bread.
tips: Soak beans for 6–8 hours, rinse and drain; overnight soaking helps plan the cooking.
Cook poultry to at least 74°C in the thickest section; use a food thermometer when available.
search_terms: chicken served with rice or bread
ga-nau-dau.image_alt: Chicken stew with red beans, soybeans and carrot in a lightly thickened broth.
ga-nau-dau.time_note: About 7 hours 55 minutes including 6 hours to soak beans and 15 minutes to marinate.

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.notes: Cut into serving pieces; thighs or wings stay tender.

ingredients.name: Dried soybeans
ingredients.notes: Soak 6–8 hours, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Dried red beans
ingredients.notes: Soak 6–8 hours, rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For browning chicken and sauteing garlic.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add hot water if needed.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Divide between marinade and broth.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to balance seasoning.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Divide between marinade and garnish.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice.

preparation_steps: Soak soybeans and red beans separately for 6–8 hours; rinse and drain.
Rinse and drain chicken, cut into pieces and marinate with some garlic, seasoning powder, pepper and sugar for 15 minutes.
Peel and cut carrot; mince remaining garlic and rinse and slice scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
cooking_steps: Heat oil and brown chicken on all sides; set aside.
Saute remaining garlic, return chicken, add soaked beans and about 700 ml water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer until beans are nearly tender, adding hot water if needed.
Add carrot and cook about 10 minutes until just tender. Season, ensure chicken is fully cooked, then turn off the heat.
Finish with scallions, Vietnamese coriander and pepper. Serve with rice or bread.
ga-nau-dau.media_alt_text: A bowl of chicken stew with red and soy beans, carrot and a lightly thickened broth.

canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.name: Amaranth soup with dried shrimp
aliases: Red amaranth soup with dried shrimp
Vietnamese amaranth and dried shrimp soup
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.serving_basis: One pot of red amaranth soup with dried shrimp for four people.
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.description: Young red amaranth simmers briefly with softened dried shrimp, giving the soup a gentle savory flavor and natural rosy hue. This simple Bếp Việt version suits an everyday rice meal.
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.finished_dish: Clear, gently savory broth with tender red amaranth that keeps its natural color and is not overcooked.
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.serving: Ladle into bowls and serve hot with rice; avoid prolonged boiling once the greens are tender.
tips: Soak dried shrimp until soft, then lightly pound so its flavor infuses the broth.
Add amaranth once the broth boils and cook only until tender.
search_terms: red amaranth and dried shrimp soup
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.image_alt: A bowl of red amaranth soup with softened dried shrimp in a light rosy broth.
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.time_note: About 35 minutes including 10 minutes to soak the shrimp; cook greens only until tender.

ingredients.name: Red amaranth
ingredients.notes: Choose young leaves and tender stems; rinse well.

ingredients.name: Dried shrimp
ingredients.notes: Soak in warm water, drain and lightly pound.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For briefly sauteing shrimp.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the preferred soup consistency.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly because dried shrimp may be salty.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add near the end and adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle lightly before serving.

preparation_steps: Soak dried shrimp in warm water for about 10 minutes, drain and lightly pound.
Remove old amaranth leaves, rinse thoroughly and drain; cut long stems into bite-size lengths.
cooking_steps: Heat a little oil and briefly saute shrimp until fragrant.
Add water, bring to a boil and skim any foam. Season lightly.
Add amaranth and cook just until tender. Season with fish sauce and salt, turn off the heat and finish with pepper.
canh-rau-den-nau-tom-kho.media_alt_text: A bowl of red amaranth soup with softened dried shrimp in a light broth.
